summary: Appeals challenge High Court conviction for murder under Sections 302/396 IPC after trial court acquitted for murder but convicted for robbery under Section 392 IPC; prosecution relied on circumstantial evidence including jeep seizure, police recovery of weapons, and confession of accused A1; key issues: scope of appellate review in cases of trial court acquittal, reliability of circumstantial evidence and confession; High Court convicted based on circumstantial evidence but failed to establish two views test or perversity in trial court findings; prosecution shortcomings: no proof of vehicle ownership, lack of FSL examination on incriminating articles, omission of vehicle registration in police communication; confession of A1 inadmissible against co-accused under Sections 25-26 Evidence Act; appeals allowed restoring trial court acquittal on murder charges.
legal_provisions_cited: Indian Penal Code, 1860 s.302, s.34, s.392, s.396, s.397
final_judgment: Appeals allowed; High Court judgment reversed; trial court acquittal on Sections 302/34, 396, and 397 IPC restored; Section 392 IPC conviction for robbery maintained.
